set.seed(42)

#### Import landmarks and specimen information ####

tps_file = "data/All_sections.TPS"

# Import landmarks from TPS file
landmarks <- geomorph::readland.tps(tps_file, specID = "ID", readcurves = TRUE)
## 
##  141 curve points detected per specimen and are appended to fixed landmarks.
# Import specimen information from CSV
specimen_info <- read.csv("data/Specimens_info.csv", header = TRUE)

#### Data cleaning and preparation ####

specimen_info$Region <- trimws(specimen_info$Region)

# Clean specimen IDs: trim whitespace and unify case
specimen_info$ID <- specimen_info$ID %>% 
  trimws() %>% 
  toupper()

tps_ids <- dimnames(landmarks)[[3]] %>% 
  trimws() %>% 
  toupper()

dimnames(landmarks)[[3]] <- tps_ids

# Check for unmatched specimen IDs
missing_in_csv <- tps_ids[!tps_ids %in% specimen_info$ID]
missing_in_tps <- specimen_info$ID[!specimen_info$ID %in% tps_ids]

if (length(missing_in_csv) > 0) {
  cat("TPS specimen IDs NOT found in Specimens_info.csv:\n")
  print(missing_in_csv)
}

if (length(missing_in_tps) > 0) {
  cat("Specimens_info.csv IDs NOT found in TPS:\n")
  print(missing_in_tps)
}

# Stop if any missing IDs to avoid misalignment
if (length(missing_in_csv) > 0 || length(missing_in_tps) > 0) {
  stop("Mismatch between TPS IDs and specimen_info IDs. Please fix and rerun.")
}

# Match specimen_info order to TPS specimen IDs
match_rows <- match(tps_ids, specimen_info$ID)
specimen_info_matched <- specimen_info[match_rows, ]
rm(tps_ids)
rm(missing_in_csv)
rm(missing_in_tps)
rm(match_rows)


#### Geometric morphometric preprocessing ####

# Define sliding landmarks
sliders <- geomorph::define.sliders(3:138)
# Perform Generalized Procrustes Analysis (GPA)
landmarks.gpa <- geomorph::gpagen(landmarks, curves = sliders)
## 
## Performing GPA
##   |                                                                              |                                                                      |   0%  |                                                                              |=======                                                               |  10%
## Singular BE matrix; using generalized inverse  |                                                                              |==============                                                        |  20%

## Singular BE matrix; using generalized inverse  |                                                                              |===============================================================       |  90%
## Singular BE matrix; using generalized inverse  |                                                                              |======================================================================| 100%
## 
## Making projections... Finished!
# Perform PCA on GPA-aligned coordinates
PCA <- geomorph::gm.prcomp(landmarks.gpa$coords)
plot(PCA, main = "Principal Component Analysis of Morphological Variation")

Principal component analysis (PCA) of Pseudofurnishius murcianus morphological variation based on informative principal components. 

# Calculate mean shape

#### Calculate mean distances and combine data ####

source("src/calculate_distance.R")
source("src/process_data.R")

lengths <- process_data(tps_file)

# Combine all data
data_combined <- specimen_info_matched %>%
  dplyr::left_join(lengths, by = "ID")

# Add PCA scores
data_combined$PC1 <- PCA$x[, 1]
data_combined$PC2 <- PCA$x[, 2]
data_combined$PC3 <- PCA$x[, 3]
data_combined$PC4 <- PCA$x[, 4]
data_combined$PC5 <- PCA$x[, 5]
data_combined$PC6 <- PCA$x[, 6]
data_combined$PC7 <- PCA$x[, 7]

all_pcs <- PCA$x
# After GUENSER et al., 2022
doPcaSignif <- function(eigvals) {
  
  acron <- character()
  criterion <- character()
  nsigncomp <- numeric()
  n <- length(eigvals)
  
  # Percentage variance explained
  pcvars <- 100 * eigvals / sum(eigvals)
  
  # Broken stick model
  bsm <- data.frame(j = seq_len(n), p = 0)
  bsm$p[1] <- 1 / n
  for(i in 2:n){
    bsm$p[i] <- bsm$p[i - 1] + (1 / (n + 1 - i))
  }
  bsm$p <- 100 * bsm$p / n
  bsvars <- rev(bsm$p)
  
  acron <- "BSM"
  criterion <- "Broken stick model"
  nsigncomp <- sum(pcvars >= bsvars)
  
  data.frame(acron, criterion, nsigncomp)
}

# Eigenvalues from your geomorph PCA
pcasign <- doPcaSignif(PCA$d^2)

print(pcasign)
##   acron          criterion nsigncomp
## 1   BSM Broken stick model         6
# Plot Eigenvalues of first 20 PCs, to visualise
eigvals_all <- (PCA$d)^2

# Number of PCs to display
npcs <- min(20, length(eigvals_all))

eigvals <- eigvals_all[1:npcs]

# % variance explained
pcvars <- 100 * eigvals / sum(eigvals_all)

# Broken-stick expectations
n <- length(eigvals_all)

bsvars_all <- sapply(1:n, function(i) {
  100 * sum(1/(i:n))/n
})

bsvars <- bsvars_all[1:npcs]
plot(pcvars, type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Principal Component",
     ylab = "Variance explained (%)",
     xlim = c(1, npcs),
     ylim = c(0, max(pcvars, bsvars) * 1.05),
     main = "Scree Plot with Broken Stick Model")

lines(bsvars, type = "b", pch = 16, col = "red", lwd = 2)
legend("topright",
       legend = c("Observed", "Broken stick"),
       fill = c("lightgrey", NA),
       border = c("black", NA),
       lty = c(NA, 1),
       pch = c(NA, 16),
       col = c("black", "red"))

Scree Plot with Broken Stick Model

data_combined <- cbind(
  data_combined,

)

data_combined$Region[data_combined$Section %in% c("Prikrnica", "Drežnica")] <- "Northeastern"

  Section = c(
    "Henarejos" = "#fc8d59", 
    "Libros" = "#fee090",
    "Bugarra" = "#ffffbf",
    "Prikrnica" = "darkblue",

# Create chirality grouping factor  
specimen_info_matched$Chirality <- factor(ifelse(specimen_info_matched$Chirality == "R", "Dextral", "Sinistral"))

#### Save all processed data and objects ####
save(
  landmarks, specimen_info_matched, landmarks.gpa, PCA, msho,
  data_combined, colors_list, 
  file = "data/processed_data.RData"
)

After importing the data and performing Principal Component Analysis, we examined which PCs were informative. This was achieved by a Broken-Stick Model (BSM; Barton & David 1956; Frontier 1976, using a code by Guenser et al. 2022) It turned out that, in our case, the first six PCs were informative.

Folowing tabel show how much % each PC is explainig.

Principal Component Variance explained (%) Cumulative variance explained (%)
PC1 26.84% 26.84%
PC2 20.23% 47.07%
PC3 11.82% 58.90%
PC4 7.98% 66.87%
PC5 5.08% 71.96%
PC6 4.74% 76.69%

Statistical test of normality

shapiro.test(data_combined$Length)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  data_combined$Length
## W = 0.94351, p-value = 2.761e-15
data_combined %>%
  group_by(Chirality) %>%
  summarise(
    W = shapiro.test(as.numeric(Length))$statistic,
    p_value = shapiro.test(as.numeric(Length))$p.value
  )
## # A tibble: 2 × 3
##   Chirality     W  p_value
##   <fct>     <dbl>    <dbl>

data_combined %>%

Regardless of whether we analyse length as a variable across the entire dataset or within individual groups (chirality, regions and section), it does not follow a normal distribution, as all p-values of Shapiro test are lower than 0.05.

# The number of analysed sinistral elements differed between section, and resampling method was employed
sin_data <- subset(data_combined, Chirality == "Sinistral")
run_Section_dispersion <- function(df, n_sample = 10){
  
  replicate(500, {
    
    keep <- unlist(
      lapply(levels(df$Section), function(reg){
        
        idx <- which(df$Section == reg)
        
        if(length(idx) > n_sample){
          sample(idx, n_sample)
        } else {
          idx
        }
        
      })
    )
    
    bd <- betadisper(
      dist(df[keep, paste0("PC",1:7)]),
      group = df$Section[keep]
    )
    
    test <- permutest(
      bd,
      permutations = 999
    )
    
    test$tab$`Pr(>F)`[1]
    
  })
}


set.seed(42)
results_sin_disp_sect <- run_Section_dispersion(sin_data)

mean(results_sin_disp_sect < 0.05)
## [1] 0.018

The difference in multivariate dispersion remained significant only in low number of % of iterations, indication that disparity within section is highly dependent on sample size.

# The number of analysed dextral elements differed between section, and resampling method was employed
dex_data <- subset(data_combined, Chirality == "Dextral")

run_Section_dispersion_dex <- function(df, n_sample = 8){
  
  replicate(500, {
    
    keep <- unlist(
      lapply(levels(df$Section), function(reg){
        
        idx <- which(df$Section == reg)
        
        if(length(idx) > n_sample){
          sample(idx, n_sample)
        } else {
          idx
        }
        
      })
    )
    
    bd <- betadisper(
      dist(df[keep, paste0("PC",1:7)]),
      group = df$Section[keep]
    )
    
    test <- permutest(
      bd,
      permutations = 999
    )
    
    test$tab$`Pr(>F)`[1]
    
  })
}


set.seed(42)
results_dex_disp_sect <- run_Section_dispersion_dex(dex_data)

mean(results_dex_disp_sect < 0.05)
## [1] 0.004

The difference in multivariate dispersion remained significant in low % of iterations. Observed regional differences and higher morphological variability of NE likely occur because of sample size between section.

Analyses

Length

Chirality

stats::kruskal.test(Length ~ Chirality, data = data_combined)
## 
##  Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test
## 
## data:  Length by Chirality
## Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 1.6926, df = 1, p-value = 0.1933
aggregate(Length ~ Chirality, data = data_combined, mean)
##   Chirality   Length
## 1 Sinistral 402.7021
## 2   Dextral 394.9000

Based on Kruskal Wallis test the difference in length between sinistral and dextral is not significant so, we will group them all together when comparing length between different groups (region, section).

Section

##     Section   Length
## 1 Henarejos 403.3613

## 3   Bugarra 394.1093
## 4 Prikrnica 403.8841
## 5  Drežnica 386.8302
kruskal.test(Length ~ Section, data = data_combined)
##

dunn.test(data_combined$Length, g=data_combined$Section, method="bonferroni")
##   Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test
## 
## data: x and group
## Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 6.1269, df = 4, p-value = 0.19
## 
## 
##                            Comparison of x by group                            
##                                  (Bonferroni)                                  
## Col Mean-|
## Row Mean |    Bugarra   Drežnica   Henarejo     Libros
## ---------+--------------------------------------------
## Drežnica |   1.582179
##          |     0.5680
##          |
## Henarejo |   0.941654  -0.765290
##          |     1.0000     1.0000
##          |
##   Libros |  -0.725722  -1.828599  -1.290568
##          |     1.0000     0.3373     0.9843
##          |
## Prikrnic |  -1.123353  -1.975312  -1.487755  -0.119266
##          |     1.0000     0.2412     0.6841     1.0000
## 
## alpha = 0.05
## Reject Ho if p <= alpha/2

Based on Kruskal Wallis test the difference in length between section is not significant. Pairwise post hoc comparisons using Dunn’s test with Bonferroni correction further supported this result, as none of the pairwise comparisons between sections are statistically significant.

plot_distance_violin <- function(data, group_var, colors, title = NULL) {
  ggplot(data, aes_string(x = group_var, y = "Length", fill = group_var)) +
    geom_violin(alpha = 0.7, trim = FALSE) +
    geom_boxplot(
      width = 0.15,
      alpha = 0.8,
      outlier.shape = 16,
      outlier.size = 1.5
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colors) +
    labs(
      x = group_var,
      y = "Length [μm]",
      title = title
    ) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
    )
}

# The number of analysed sinistral elements differed between section, and resampling method was employed

run_Section_test <- function(df, n_sample = 10){
  
  replicate(500, {
    
    keep <- unlist(
      lapply(levels(df$Section), function(sec){
        
        idx <- which(df$Section == sec)
        
        if(length(idx) > n_sample){
          sample(idx, n_sample)
        } else {
          idx
        }
        
      })
    )
    
    test <- adonis2(
      dist(df[keep, paste0("PC",1:7)]) ~ Section,
      data = df[keep, ],
      permutations = 999
    )
    
    test$`Pr(>F)`[1]
    
  })
}


results_sin_section <- run_Section_test(sin_data)

mean(results_sin_section < 0.05)
## [1] 0.146

Sinistral elements significantly differ in shape among sections. To evaluate whether the differences in morphological variability were associated with unequal sam-ple size among sections, in 500 iterations, specimens were randomly subsampled within each section (10 samples per section) and differences in multivariate dispersion and average shape configuration were reassessed.

A resampling approach showed the differences of multivariate shape between section is present in low % % of 500 iteration. Therefore, differences in average shape configuration, when considering sample size, are not significant between sections.

Dextral elements shape differs significantly among sections. However here to the sample size varies between section.

A resampling approach applied to PERMANOVA showed that differences of dextral elements in multivariate shape among sections remains significant in high % of 500 iteration. Consequently, the observed differences among sections reflect average shape configuration.

mean_shape_Dextral <- geomorph::mshape(landmarks.gpa$coords[, , specimen_info_matched$Chirality == "Dextral"])



plot(
  mean_shape_Sinistral[,1],
  mean_shape_Sinistral[,2],
  asp = 1,
  type = "n",
  xlab = "X",
  ylab = "Y"
)
points(mean_shape_Sinistral[,1], mean_shape_Sinistral[,2],
       pch=21, bg="black")

points(mean_shape_Dextral[,1], mean_shape_Dextral[,2],
       pch=21, bg="grey")

legend(
  "topright",
  legend=c("Sinistral","Dextral"),
  pch=21,
  pt.bg=c("black","grey")
)
